ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct, dark reticulated pattern on its back and limbs. Key features include a pointed snout and prominent, longitudinal skin ridges.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ingerana reticulata* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark, net-like reticulations covering its venter, which are absent in other similar Indian ground frogs.
ai.habitat: *Ingerana reticulata* inhabits the leaf litter of primary evergreen tropical rainforests in the Western Ghats, typically at mid-to-high altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ingerana reticulata* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky substrates of its forest stream habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ingerana reticulata* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of pigmented eggs in terrestrial nests near water, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ingerana reticulata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ingerana reticulata* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard near small streams in lowland rainforests.
